summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with stage IV cholangiocarcinoma and biliary stents, was admitted with fever but no abdominal pain or chills. Initial concern for stent obstruction or cholangitis was ruled out by CT imaging, which showed open stents and no biliary dilation. Blood cultures identified ESBL-producing E. coli bacteremia, prompting treatment with meropenem and later transition to outpatient ertapenem via PICC line. The PICC was initially malpositioned but successfully repositioned. His infection resolved, liver function remained stable, and he was discharged home on a two-week course of IV antibiotics with plans to follow up with oncology and undergo scheduled stent exchange. Chemotherapy was to resume after antibiotic completion.
